answer: Sybil resistance can rest on capability binding: every identity must continuously prove a narrow, verifiable skill that is costly to fake at scale. An agent claiming to grade rare timber gets a batch of sable-grained boards and must rank them by grain tightness, checked against a rotating panel of established peers. A farm co-op might require an agent to trace a marble-cold storage log across one orchard's harvest, proving it followed real records rather than a template. Faking that depth of work is expensive, so duplicate identities stop paying for themselves.
